description:
BOARD REQUEST (DM conversation 7, msg 555, 2026-09-07): 'I'd like to see the app in action, can you make me a demo?' Filed by the CTO on the board's behalf; the demo's shape below is the CTO's decision.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, honestly. On master, apps/invoicing is a complete v1 SERVER: accounts + sessions + route guard (AS-40), Stripe Connect onboarding (AS-41), contract templates and generation (AS-42), client creation (AS-65), the invoice lifecycle — customer mirror, draft, finalize, send (AS-43), and the webhook receiver with signature verification, idempotency and invoice state sync (AS-44). It has NO user interface on master: views/ holds only the AS-37 scaffold page. Screen 1 of 7 (sign up / sign in, AS-45) exists on the unmerged branch feat/AS-45-onboarding-ui and is one review cycle from merge. Screens 2-7 (Connect Stripe AS-70, dashboard + invoice detail AS-48, invoice create/edit AS-46, contract create/detail AS-47) are not built. There is NO Stripe test-mode account — AS-51 is still needs_human on the board's desk — so every external call in this demo goes to stripe-mock (stateless, shape-validating, emits no webhooks) on the local compose stack. Every processor/ESP/carrier signup is board-gated (CLAUDE.md, Product), and this task opens NOTHING: no account, no key, no host, no spend.

WHAT THE DEMO IS. Two deliverables, one reproducible and one viewable.

(1) apps/invoicing/demo/: a scripted, deterministic walkthrough that a human runs with two commands (docker compose up, then node demo/run.mjs from the host — plain fetch, zero new dependencies, driving the app's own HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:8348 exactly as a browser would). It seeds a named demo freelancer and client with fixed values, then walks the Rule-1 chain in order and PRINTS what it does and what it got back, annotated in plain language: sign up -> session cookie -> start Connect onboarding (stripe-mock returns a Stripe-shaped account_link URL; the demo says so and does not pretend a hosted round trip happened) -> readiness snapshot seeded to 'ready' by the same path the suite uses -> create a client -> generate a contract from a template and show the rendered document -> draft an invoice with line items in integer minor units -> finalize -> send -> deliver a SYNTHESIZED, correctly signed invoice.paid webhook to POST /webhooks/stripe -> read the invoice back as paid. The transcript must label every step as one of: 'real app behaviour', 'stripe-mock stand-in', or 'synthesized event' — the board should never have to guess which is which. Idempotent: re-running from a fresh volume gives a byte-comparable transcript modulo ids and timestamps.

(2) A captured artifact the board views without running anything: a single static HTML page holding the annotated transcript plus screenshots of screen 1 (sign-in and sign-up modes, at 375px and a desktop width, plus one validation-error state) rendered from the merged AS-45 code. Publish it the way the company already publishes viewable artifacts — the brand-artifact and wireframe-artifact skills each publish one static page to a hosted Artifact; follow that precedent (a build script under .claude/skills/, one artifact URL file, republish to the same URL). That precedent is established and board-viewed, so it is not a new external service; if the implementer finds it requires any new account or service, STOP and route to needs_human rather than opening one. Screenshots are taken from the local compose stack by whatever the implementer can run locally with no new dependency in apps/invoicing (a headless browser on the host is acceptable capture tooling; it must not enter the app's image or lockfile — LOCK_ENTRIES=70 and DIRECT_DEPENDENCIES=['ejs','express'] do not move).

WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT SHOW, to be stated verbatim at the top of the artifact. CAN: the whole server-side core loop working end to end on this codebase, one real screen in a real browser, the contract document the app generates, the custody guard (never in the flow of funds — the demo shows the platform key never charging anyone). CANNOT: screens 2-7 (not built); a real Stripe onboarding round trip, a real hosted invoice page, a real payment, or a real webhook (no test-mode account — AS-51); email of any kind (no ESP by design). The paid state at the end of the transcript is produced by an event WE signed, which proves our receiver and state machine, not Stripe's delivery.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not AS-49 (the automated end-to-end loop with a STATEFUL Stripe double). AS-49 is a TEST with a red/green verdict inside the suite; this is a NARRATED WALKTHROUGH for a human, run from the host, outside the suite, against stripe-mock only. They drive the same chain, so the demo script must be written so AS-49's planner can lift its request sequence, and it must not grow assertions, a fake, or a verdict — the moment it wants to assert, that assertion belongs in AS-49. It is also not the acceptance run (AS-50). Not in this task: any new screen; any change to routes, lib, views or tests in apps/invoicing beyond what capture needs (expected: none); a hosted deployment of the app itself (Digital Ocean is a separate, board-gated step).

DEPENDENCY. depends_on AS-45: the only screen the demo can show lives on that branch, and building the artifact against an unmerged branch would publish screenshots of code that can still change. AS-45 is a two-line rework from merge (cycle 4 authorized 2026-09-07). Nothing else gates this: no AS-51, no AS-49, no AS-70. When later screens merge, the demo is re-run and re-captured — the reproducible half is the point; the artifact is a snapshot of it.

VERIFICATION: (a) a fresh clone + docker compose up + the one host command produces the full transcript with exit 0 and every step labelled; (b) the network-off suite and the contract suite are unchanged and green (the demo adds nothing to either); (c) the artifact page opens at its URL and matches the transcript the reviewer generates independently (ids/timestamps aside); (d) the reviewer confirms by grep that the artifact's 'cannot' list is present and true — a demo that overclaims is the failure mode here.

BOARD GATES HIT: none, so long as it stays on stripe-mock, local compose, and the existing artifact precedent. Ticks: ~3 (plan, implement, review) after AS-45 merges.
title: D1 demo for the board: scripted local-compose walkthrough of the v1 core loop + a viewable captured artifact
